title: FIFA Eyes Record 64-Team World Cup for 2030 as CONMEBOL Chief Confirms Expansion Plan
excerpt: CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez says the 2030 centenary tournament in Spain, Portugal and Morocco will feature 64 nations, up from 48 in 2026.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • CONMEBOL president endorses a 64-team World Cup for 2030 to celebrate its centenary.
  • FIFA president plans to discuss expansion after the 2026 World Cup concludes.
  • The new format could increase Asian slots to 11-12, enhancing India's qualification chances.
  • Critics argue the expansion may dilute match quality, but FIFA's revenue supports it.
  • FIFA's revenue for 2023-2026 is projected at nearly $14 billion, bolstering expansion arguments.

Asian Slots in 2026
  • CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez publicly endorsed a 64-team 2030 World Cup to mark the tournament's centenary
  • FIFA president Gianni Infantino said discussions on expansion would begin after the 2026 tournament concluded
  • A 64-team format would mean 16 groups of four, 128 matches, and potentially 11-12 slots for Asian nations — boosting India's qualification prospects
  • Critics warn the change could dilute quality, but FIFA's record $14 billion revenue from the 2026 cycle makes further expansion all but inevitable

The 2026 FIFA World Cup is barely over, and football's governing bodies are already pushing to make the next edition even bigger. CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez declared on social media that the 2030 tournament — to be hosted across Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay — will feature 64 teams, up from the 48-team format that debuted this summer.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DbCB5iJC-JV/ > **"The Asian Football Confederation received eight slots at the 2026 World Cup."**

"In 2030, the World Cup is coming to Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. A great opportunity for football, to celebrate the Centenary of the World Cup with a 64-team tournament."

— Alejandro Dominguez, CONMEBOL President

What a 64-Team Tournament Would Look Like

Under the proposed format, the World Cup would expand to 16 groups of four teams, up from the 12 groups used in 2026. Each team would still play three group matches, but only the top two from each group would advance to a round of 32, eliminating the complicated best-third-place finisher system that drew criticism at this year's tournament.

https://x.com/FIFAcom/status/2078982201803223364

The total number of matches would rise to 128, compared to 104 in 2026 and 64 in the traditional 32-team format. Crucially, individual teams would not face additional games — still playing a maximum of eight matches from group stage through the final.

India's Qualifying Hopes Could Brighten

For India and other developing football nations across Asia, the expansion could be transformative. The Asian Football Confederation received eight slots at the 2026 World Cup. Under a 64-team model, projections suggest Asia could receive 11 to 12 berths, according to USA Today. That nearly 50 percent increase would significantly improve the chances of nations like India, Bahrain and Thailand, which have historically fallen just short of qualification.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5S-MQXH1BQU

India has never qualified for a World Cup through the standard process, with its sole appearance coming in 1950 when the team withdrew. The 140th-ranked side would remain a long shot even with expanded slots, but a larger Asian allocation would at least make the dream mathematically plausible.

The Money Speaks Louder Than the Critics

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has publicly opposed the idea, calling it "a bad idea" as early as April 2025. Purists argue that some group-stage matches at the 2026 tournament already lacked intensity, with several lower-ranked sides struggling to compete.

Financial Justification for Expansion
›FIFA's revenue for 2023-2026 is nearly $14 billion.
›2026 World Cup set attendance record with 6.81 million fans.
›Critics warn of diluted quality, but financial gains are significant.
Source: Kieran Maguire, football finance expert

But the financial arithmetic favours expansion. FIFA's revenue across the 2023-2026 cycle is estimated at nearly $14 billion, according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire, with the 2026 World Cup alone setting an all-time attendance record of 6.81 million fans across the United States, Canada and Mexico.

"When organizing a World Cup, it's important to organize it for the whole world — not just Europe and South America. Every nation should be allowed to dream of participating in the World Cup."

— Gianni Infantino, FIFA President

What Happens Next

FIFA has not formally approved the expansion. Infantino told media outlets that the governing body would evaluate the proposal after the 2026 tournament's conclusion. Dominguez's comments, however, carry weight — he serves as a FIFA vice president and Council member.

The 2030 World Cup is already the most complex in history, spanning six host nations across three continents. Adding 16 more teams would require additional venues, training facilities and accommodation across Morocco, Portugal and Spain, the primary hosts. Qualification pathways for all six confederations would also need to be recalibrated.

A final decision is expected within the next 12 months, with FIFA's Congress likely to vote on the matter by early 2027.

![Gianni Infantino. Every nation should be allowed to dream of participating in the World Cup." — Gianni Infantino, FIFA President What Happens Next FIFA has not formally approved the expansion.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ac/Gianni_Infantino_-_55062516828.jpg)
nri_angle: An expanded 64-team World Cup could give India its most realistic path to qualification in history, and would energize football development across South Asia.
